subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Spark Ignition
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Spark Ignition.

hook.text: A spark plug fires a tiny bolt of electricity across a gap smaller than a coin's edge.

buildup.text: That spark must ignite a precise fuel-air mix at exactly the right moment in the cycle.

discovery.text: Fire too early and the engine knocks—fire too late and power is wasted as heat.

twist.text: Modern ignition timing adjusts hundreds of times per second based on speed, load, and temperature.

climax.text: Switching from mechanical distributors to electronic ignition gave engines 20 percent more efficiency.

punchline.text: A spark the size of a pinhead powers a two-ton machine.

quiz.question: What happens when spark timing is too early?

details.summary: Spark plugs deliver a precisely timed electrical arc of up to 40,000 volts across a tiny gap to ignite the compressed air-fuel mixture in each cylinder, initiating the controlled explosion that powers the engine.
details.whyItMatters: Spark timing is critical to engine performance. Millisecond-precise ignition determines power output, emissions, and efficiency. Modern engines adjust timing thousands of times per second for optimal combustion.
takeaways: Spark plugs fire at up to 40,000 volts to ignite the fuel mixture
Timing must be precise to within a fraction of a millisecond
Advanced ignition systems vary timing based on load, speed, and knock

faq.question: Why does spark timing change with engine speed?
faq.answer: At higher RPM, the piston moves faster so the spark must fire earlier to allow the flame front time to fully burn the mixture before the piston descends. This is called ignition advance and is managed electronically.

faq.question: How long do modern spark plugs last?
faq.answer: Iridium and platinum spark plugs typically last 60,000 to 100,000 miles. Older copper plugs needed replacement every 20,000 to 30,000 miles. Some high-performance applications still prefer copper for its superior conductivity.
